takeaway: Dry season is locked in. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has clear, sunny, breezy weather on the North Pacific all day today, with Nicoya near 34°C and no rain chance. The strong gusts from earlier this week have eased to occasional gusts near the mountains, mostly early in the day. For surf, the Caribbean trade winds stay offshore at Nosara. They are steady today through Monday, ease to their lightest Tuesday and Wednesday, then build again from about Friday Nov 27 into early December. Dawn to late morning is the best window every day. No rainy spell and no tropical storm threat for the next two weeks.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sat Nov 21 – Mon Nov 23)
periods.pattern: High pressure over northern Central America keeps a steady east-northeast trade wind flowing across Nicaragua and Guanacaste. IMN calls Saturday clear and windy on the North Pacific from dawn to night, with the only rain chance in the country on the South Pacific mountains in the afternoon. Both main models and all three ensemble averages show that steady trade-wind stream through Monday. The rain maps keep Nicoya at a trace or less each day, with the light showers on the Caribbean side.
periods.implications: Sunny and hot, around 34°C in the afternoon and near 21°C at night. Breezy, but less gusty than earlier in the week. A great weekend for anything outdoors. Pack sun protection and water, not rain gear.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Tue Nov 24 – Fri Nov 27)
periods.pattern: A short lull. The marine forecast drops the Papagayo winds to about 10–15 knots from the east Monday night and Tuesday, then about 10 knots from the north to northeast on Tuesday night and Wednesday. Around Wednesday, the European model shows a strong north wind surge into the southern Gulf of Mexico. Surges like that often come before stronger Caribbean trades a couple of days later, and the ensemble averages bring the trades back up by Friday. IMN's weekly outlook (Nov 19–25) keeps Guanacaste clear and very hot, with highs up to 37°C in the region during the lighter-wind days. The rain maps still keep Nicoya dry.
periods.implications: The hottest, stickiest days of the stretch, especially Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons with less breeze. Calm water makes these the best days for boat, paddle, or fishing trips. A stray afternoon shower is possible over the hills inland, but rain at the beach is unlikely.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate on how light the wind gets midweek and when it picks back up.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Sat Nov 28 – Sat Dec 5)
periods.pattern: A classic dry-season trade-wind pattern. All three ensemble averages show a stronger east-northeast wind stream across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica from about Nov 28 to Dec 1, and the trades are still blowing through Dec 5. That wind brings rain to the Caribbean side: the American and European ensemble averages put about 0.5–1 inch in a day on Costa Rica's and southern Nicaragua's Caribbean coast in the 24 hours ending the evenings of Fri Nov 27 and Sun Nov 29. Nicoya stays at a trace to about 0.05 inch a day. The European ensemble average shows a weak low just off southern Costa Rica and Panama on Dec 1. That's the usual low that forms downwind of the mountains when trades blow hard, not a storm. IMN's sub-seasonal outlook has the North Pacific at 0–50 mm for each of the weeks of Nov 23–29 and Nov 30–Dec 6, with a low chance of extreme rain and below-normal rain countrywide.
periods.implications: Plan freely. Expect sunny, windy, dusty days and warm, breezy nights. Tie down loose gear and be careful with fire once the trades pick back up. Boat trips will be rougher around Nov 28 to Dec 1.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate on the timing and strength of the trade-wind push.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trade winds (east-northeast), offshore at Nosara, all period. Steady today through Monday, lightest Tuesday and Wednesday, then stronger from about Fri Nov 27 through Dec 1. No Pacific onshore pattern in sight.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued about 2:40 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds of 15–20 knots offshore in the Gulf of Papagayo today through Sunday night (10–15 knots elsewhere), 15–20 knots Monday, east 10–15 knots Monday night and Tuesday, then north to northeast around 10 knots Tuesday night and Wednesday. It says the winds pulse strongest each night. Off the Nicoya coast and south, winds stay light and variable (under 5 knots), so the offshore breeze reaches Nosara over the land, not along the coast. Swell (open-ocean numbers, not beach heights): south to southwest 4–7 ft at 14–16 seconds through Wednesday, bumping to 5–7 ft at 16 seconds south of the peninsula on Tuesday. Nicaragua should be offshore all day through Monday, which points to clean Nosara mornings. That doesn't mean all day offshore here: the afternoon sea breeze can turn it side-on. During the Tuesday–Wednesday lull, expect the morning offshore to be lighter and the sea breeze to arrive earlier.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today through Monday: dawn to late morning. It may stay clean past noon on the windier days. Tuesday and Wednesday: dawn to mid-morning, then likely bumpy from the sea breeze. Nov 27 to Dec 1: dawn to late morning, and offshore could hold most of the day, though gusty.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings all period. Moderate on afternoon sea-breeze timing and strength at the beach.

gyreWatch.status: Not established. No watch needed. No prolonged rainy spell expected.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Nothing organized through about Dec 5. The global tropics outlook (issued Nov 17, next update Tue Nov 24) gives a small chance (under 20%) of a storm forming somewhere in the eastern Pacific in late November or early December. It's a long shot, not aimed at Costa Rica.
gyreWatch.supporting: Very little. The global outlook still mentions that small storm chance. The European ensemble average shows a weak low off southern Costa Rica and Panama on Dec 1, but it sits under strong offshore trades, so it reads as a downwind low, not a developing storm.
gyreWatch.conflicting: The evidence against is strong. Trades push the rain to the Caribbean side, and all three ensemble averages keep Nicoya at a trace to 0.05 inch a day through Dec 5. The hurricane center expects no tropical storm formation in the next 7 days and shows no disturbances. IMN's sub-seasonal outlook calls the dry season established, with below-normal rain and a low chance of extreme events. The global outlook favors below-normal rain for parts of Central America during a strong El Niño.

whatChanged: Since the last published briefing (Wed Nov 18; the Nov 19 and 20 updates didn't run): The windy spell eased as expected. IMN no longer calls for 40–60 km/h gusts and now has only occasional gusts near the mountains, mostly early. The weekend trades are a bit stronger than expected: the marine forecast now keeps 15–20 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo through Monday, up from the 10–15 knots it showed for Saturday night and Sunday. The new outlook adds a light-wind lull Tuesday and Wednesday. The renewed trade-wind push now arrives a bit earlier, around Nov 27–Dec 1 (it was Nov 30–Dec 2). The rain outlook for Nosara hasn't changed: dry. The hurricane center still sees nothing, and the global tropics outlook hasn't been updated since Nov 17.
practical: Surf early every day. Monday's still a solid morning, and Tuesday and Wednesday need a dawn start before the sea breeze. Plan boat or paddle trips for Tuesday through Thursday, when the water is calmest. Drink plenty in 34–37°C heat, especially during the low-breeze days midweek. Tie down loose gear and be careful with fire, especially once the trades build again around Nov 27. No rain plans needed.
alerts: No active IMN warnings. The last notice, on Nov 13, was about short heavy downpours in the Central Valley and Caribbean mountains.
Marine: fresh northeast to east winds (15–20 knots) pulse each night in the Gulf of Papagayo through Monday.
